request.spec: The people, claims and pools exports taken while an as-of date is set use the as-of figures.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The people, claims and pools exports taken while an as-of date is set use the as-of figures.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The people, claims and pools exports now give the as-of figures when an as-of date is set. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

**What was wrong:** the server already answers reads for the as-of date, and the exports already build their CSVs from those reads. The problem was timing. Setting an as-of date clears all the screen's data and starts re-reading it for that date. An export pressed straight after that ran on the empty data, so the people CSV came out with only its header row.

**The fix:** all three export buttons (`export-people`, `export-claims`, `export-pools`) are now disabled while any read is in flight, using TanStack Query's `useIsFetching()`. This means an export can't be taken until the figures for the current as-of date (or for now, once it's cleared) have loaded. The test's clicks wait for the button to be enabled, so they pick this up. The change is only in the front end, in `features/people/export.slot.tsx`, `features/claims/export.slot.tsx` and `features/pools/export.slot.tsx`; nothing changed on the server, in the stored data or in the audit records.

**Side effect:** the check covers every read on the screen, not just the ones the exports use, so the buttons are also briefly disabled while anything else on the screen is loading. Nothing in the app re-reads on a timer, so this never leaves them stuck disabled.
